functions.name: RimeRegisterModule
functions.description: Registers a RimeModule with librime so it can be located and initialized by name. Typically invoked automatically via the RIME_REGISTER_MODULE/RIME_REGISTER_CUSTOM_MODULE macros during module load, but can also be called manually. The RimeModule structure may expose initialize/finalize hooks and an optional get_api function to publish custom APIs.
requirements: module must be a valid, non-null pointer to a RimeModule structure.
module->data_size should be initialized using RIME_STRUCT_INIT(RimeModule, module) before registration (as implied by the provided registration macros).
module->module_name should point to a valid null-terminated string identifying the module.
If the module relies on initialization/finalization, module->initialize and module->finalize should be valid function pointers.

functions.name: RimeFindModule
functions.description: Looks up a previously registered module by its name and returns a pointer to its RimeModule descriptor. Use this to retrieve a module’s descriptor and (optionally) its custom API via module->get_api().
requirements: module_name must be a non-null, null-terminated string matching the name supplied at registration.
Returns NULL if no module with the given name has been registered (inferred from common C API patterns).

functions.name: rime_get_api
functions.description: Acquires the version-controlled RimeApi structure containing function pointers for all public librime operations. After obtaining the pointer, clients should check availability of individual functions with RIME_API_AVAILABLE and, per the API comments, call api->setup(traits) before accessing any other API functions. The returned structure enables access to initialization, deployment, session, input/output, configuration, and utility routines.
requirements: The returned pointer should be checked for non-null before use.
Before calling any other API function pointers from the structure, call api->setup(RimeTraits*) as documented in the RimeApi comment.
Callers must check function availability with RIME_API_AVAILABLE(api, func) before invoking a function pointer from the returned structure.

functions.name: custom_settings_init
functions.signature: RimeCustomSettings* (*custom_settings_init)(const char* config_id, const char* generator_id)
functions.description: Create and return a handle for customizing settings for a specific configuration and generator. Use this handle with other custom_settings* APIs, and destroy it when done. Internal behavior and ownership of any underlying resources are not documented here.
requirements: Must be called before any other custom_settings* function for the same settings handle.
config_id must be a non-null, null-terminated C string. Exact accepted values are unknown.
generator_id must be a non-null, null-terminated C string. Exact accepted values are unknown.
Returns a non-null pointer on success; null indicates failure (exact error conditions unknown).
The returned RimeCustomSettings* must be released with custom_settings_destroy.

functions.name: custom_settings_destroy
functions.description: Destroy and release resources associated with a RimeCustomSettings handle previously created by custom_settings_init.
requirements: settings must be a non-null pointer previously returned by custom_settings_init.
Must not be called more than once on the same settings handle.
After return, the settings pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: load_settings
functions.description: Load settings associated with the provided custom settings handle, preparing it for read/write operations. Returns nonzero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: settings must be a non-null pointer initialized by custom_settings_init.
Should be called before querying or modifying settings; exact necessity is unknown.
Caller should check the Bool return value for success before proceeding.

functions.name: save_settings
functions.description: Persist changes made through the custom settings handle to storage. Returns nonzero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: settings must be a non-null pointer initialized by custom_settings_init.
If prior modifications were made, this should be called to persist them; exact persistence semantics are unknown.
Caller should check the Bool return value for success.

functions.name: customize_bool
functions.signature: Bool (*customize_bool)(RimeCustomSettings* settings, const char* key, Bool value)
functions.description: Set a boolean configuration item identified by key within the custom settings context. Returns nonzero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: settings must be a non-null pointer initialized by custom_settings_init.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated C string designating a configuration path/key. Exact key format is unknown.
value is treated as a boolean; nonzero means true, zero means false.
Caller should check the Bool return value for success.
Changes may require save_settings to persist; persistence details unknown.

functions.name: customize_int

functions.description: Set an integer configuration item identified by key. Returns nonzero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: settings must be initialized by custom_settings_init.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
value range and constraints are unknown; caller should ensure the value is appropriate for the targeted key.
Caller should check the Bool return value for success.
Call save_settings to persist changes if needed; persistence behavior unknown.

functions.name: customize_double
functions.signature: Bool (*customize_double)(RimeCustomSettings* settings, const char* key, double value)
functions.description: Set a floating-point configuration item identified by key. Returns nonzero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: settings must be initialized by custom_settings_init.
key must be non-null and null-terminated.
Value domain and precision requirements are unknown; ensure suitability for the target key.
Caller should check the Bool return value for success.
Call save_settings to persist changes if needed; persistence behavior unknown.

functions.name: customize_string
functions.signature: Bool (*customize_string)(RimeCustomSettings* settings, const char* key, const char* value)
functions.description: Set a string configuration item identified by key. Returns nonzero on success, zero on failure.
requirements: settings must be initialized by custom_settings_init.
key must be a non-null, null-terminated C string.
value must be a non-null, null-terminated C string. Encoding and maximum length are unknown.
Caller should check the Bool return value for success.
Call save_settings to persist changes if needed; persistence behavior unknown.

functions.name: is_first_run
functions.description: Indicate whether this appears to be the first run for the given settings context. Exact semantics are not documented in this header. Nonzero indicates true, zero indicates false.
requirements: settings must be initialized by custom_settings_init.
Caller should treat any nonzero as true; detailed criteria for first run are unknown.

functions.name: settings_is_modified
functions.description: Report whether the settings have been modified since load or the last save. Returns nonzero if modified, zero otherwise.
requirements: settings must be initialized by custom_settings_init.
Caller should check return value; exact definition of 'modified' is not specified.

functions.name: settings_get_config
functions.description: Expose the underlying configuration associated with the custom settings handle into a provided RimeConfig object. Returns nonzero on success. The exact ownership and lifetime rules for the populated config are not specified here.
requirements: settings must be initialized by custom_settings_init.
config must be a non-null pointer to a RimeConfig object prepared/initialized per the Rime API (exact initialization requirements unknown; see rime_api.h).
Caller must check the Bool return value before using the config.
Lifetime and mutation rules of the returned config view are unknown; avoid freeing resources not owned by the caller.

functions.name: get_available_schema_list

functions.name: get_selected_schema_list

Caller should check the Bool return value for success.

functions.name: schema_list_destroy

functions.name: user_dict_iterator_init
functions.description: Initialize an iterator for enumerating user dictionaries. On success, iter can be used with next_user_dict to traverse entries. Returns nonzero on success.

requirements: iter must be a non-null pointer that was successfully initialized by user_dict_iterator_init.
Must be called once after enumeration completes to avoid resource leaks.
After return, iter must not be used with next_user_dict unless re-initialized.

functions.name: next_user_dict
functions.description: Advance the iterator and return the next user dictionary name. Returns null when the iteration is finished or on error. The returned string is read-only.

Must not be called after user_dict_iterator_destroy.

    "switcher/hotkeys",
    "ascii_mode",
    "full_shape",
    "menu/page_size",
    "patch/key_binder/bindings",
    "key_binder/bindings/0/accept",
    "translator/dictionary",
]

HOTKEY_SAMPLES = [
    "Control+grave",
    "Shift+Space",
    "Ctrl+Shift+grave",
    "Alt+grave",
    "F4",
]

# Simple YAML snippets that are syntactically plausible for Rime configs
YAML_SNIPPETS = [
    "schema:\n  schema_id: luna_pinyin\n  name: 朙月拼音\n",
    "switcher:\n  hotkeys: [Ctrl+grave, Alt+grave]\n",
    "menu:\n  page_size: 9\n  alternative_select_keys: 1234567890\n",
    "ascii_composer:\n  switch_key:\n    Shift_L: commit_code\n    Shift_R: commit_text\n",
]

DICT_NAMES = [
    "userdict",
    "luna_pinyin.userdb",

FILE_BASENAMES = [
    "user.yaml",
    "installation.yaml",
    "default.custom.yaml",
    "schema_list.yaml",

]

DIRS = [
    "/usr/share/rime",
    "/usr/local/share/rime",
    "/opt/rime/data",
    "/tmp/rime-data",
    "/var/tmp/rime",
]

SCHEMA_IDS = [
    "luna_pinyin",
    "terra_pinyin",
    "bopomofo",
    "cangjie5",
]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_unicode(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    # mix safe ascii and chosen unicode samples
    base = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    extra = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, max_len - len(base) if max_len > len(base) else 0)
    s = base + extra
    if len(s) < min_len:
        s += _rand_ascii(rng, min_len - len(s), min_len - len(s))
    return s[:max_len]


def _rand_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build plausible absolute or relative paths without NULs
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        base = rng.choice(DIRS)
    else:
        base = "." if rng.random() < 0.5 else rng.choice(["./configs", "./schemas", "./snapshots"]) 
    parts: List[str] = []
    # 1-4 segments
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4)):
        seg = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12)
        parts.append(seg)
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        fname = rng.choice(FILE_BASENAMES)
    else:
        fname = _rand_ascii(rng, 5, 16) + rng.choice([".yaml", ".txt", ".schema.yaml"]) 
    path = base.rstrip('/') + '/' + '/'.join(parts + [fname])
    return path


def _rand_module_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(MODULE_NAME_SAMPLES)
    name = rng.choice(["rime_", "module_", "ime_"]) + _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10)
    return name


def _rand_key(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return rng.choice(KEY_SAMPLES)
    # compose nested keys like a/b/c
    depth = rng.randint(1, 3)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 12))
    return '/'.join(parts)


def _rand_hotkeys(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return ', '.join(rng.sample(HOTKEY_SAMPLES, rng.randint(1, min(3, len(HOTKEY_SAMPLES)))))
    mods = ["Ctrl", "Alt", "Shift"]
    key = rng.choice(["grave", "Space", "F1", "F2", "F3", "F4", "F5"]) 
    chosen = [m for m in mods if rng.random() < 0.5]
    return '+'.join(chosen + [key])


def _rand_yaml(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # combine snippets and add small patches for variety
    parts = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(rng.choice(YAML_SNIPPETS))
    # add random key/value
    parts.append(f"{_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10)}:\n  {_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 10)}: {_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 8)}\n")
    y = '\n'.join(parts)
    # size cap
    if len(y) > 1500:
        y = y[:1500]
    return y


def _rand_schema_list(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 4)
    ids = [rng.choice(SCHEMA_IDS) for _ in range(n)]
    return ' '.join(ids)


def _assemble_pool(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool: List[str] = []
    # Module-centric strings
    pool.append(_rand_module_name(rng))
    pool.append(_rand_module_name(rng))
    # Keys and options
    for _ in range(3):
        pool.append(_rand_key(rng))
    # Hotkeys and schema lists
    pool.append(_rand_hotkeys(rng))
    pool.append(_rand_schema_list(rng))
    # Dict names and file paths
    pool.append(rng.choice(DICT_NAMES))
    for _ in range(2):
        pool.append(_rand_path(rng))
    # YAML payload for config_load_string
    pool.append(_rand_yaml(rng))
    # Unicode-rich strings to exercise UTF-8
    pool.append(_rand_unicode(rng, 6, 40))
    # Generic ascii identifiers
    for _ in range(3):
        pool.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 20))
    # Schema ids
    pool.extend(SCHEMA_IDS)
    # App and distribution naming
    pool.append("rime.fuzzer")
    pool.append("rime.testapp")
    return pool


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    pool = _assemble_pool(rng)

    # Decide strategy: single string, concatenated with separators, or YAML
    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.35:
        s = rng.choice(pool)
    elif mode < 0.7:
        # concatenate 2-4 items with newline to serve multi-line consumers (e.g., YAML, schema IDs list)
        k = rng.randint(2, 4)
        s = '\n'.join(rng.sample(pool, k))
    else:
        s = _rand_yaml(rng)

    # Ensure not exceeding maximum size and no embedded NULs
    s = s.replace('\x00', '')
    if len(s) > MAX_SIZE - 1:
        s = s[:MAX_SIZE - 1]

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes; no trailing NUL so that fuzz framework can append as needed
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: filesystem path
# Goal: produce plausible, valid path strings that exercise different behaviors
# for FUZZ_PARAM_STR (used as directories, ids, names) and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME
# (used as writable file paths). We return bytes containing one or more newline-
# separated paths so the harness can split/consume as needed. Keep under 4096 bytes.

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."

def _rand_choice(r: random.Random, seq):
    return seq[r.randrange(len(seq))]

def _weighted(r: random.Random, items):
    # items: list of (weight, value)
    total = sum(w for w, _ in items)
    x = r.uniform(0, total)
    acc = 0.0
    for w, v in items:
        acc += w
        if x <= acc:
            return v
    return items[-1][1]

def _random_name(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    # Include some Unicode segments to exercise UTF-8 handling but keep valid
    # file names on most filesystems (avoid separators and NUL).
    unicode_pool = [
        "汉字", "日本語", "한글", "рус", "árvíztűrő", "ñandú", "🙂",
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.25:
        return _rand_choice(r, unicode_pool)
    ln = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(_rand_choice(r, SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(ln)).strip()
    # Avoid empty after strip; ensure not reserved like "." or ".."
    if not s or s in {".", ".."}:
        s = "n" + s + "x"
    return s

def _random_ext(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return _weighted(r, [
        (3, "txt"), (2, "yaml"), (2, "yml"), (2, "json"), (1, "log"),
        (1, "bin"), (1, "cfg"), (1, "ini"), (1, "schema.yaml"),
    ])

def _join_path(parts: List[str], is_windows: bool) -> str:
    sep = "\\" if is_windows else "/"
    # Avoid duplicate separators
    cleaned = []
    for p in parts:
        if p == "":
            continue
        cleaned.append(p)
    path = sep.join(cleaned)
    if is_windows:
        # Normalize occurrences like "\\." or trailing spaces
        path = path.replace("/", "\\")
    else:
        path = path.replace("//", "/")
    return path

def _random_abs_prefix(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Randomly pick POSIX, Windows drive, or UNC-like
    k = r.random()
    if k < 0.55:
        return "/"  # POSIX root
    elif k < 0.85:
        drive = chr(r.randint(ord('C'), ord('Z')))
        return f"{drive}:\\"  # Windows drive
    else:
        server = _random_name(r, 3, 8)
        share = _random_name(r, 3, 8)
        return f"\\\\{server}\\{share}\\"  # UNC

def _random_dir_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a plausible absolute or relative directory path
    is_windows = r.random() < 0.5
    parts = []
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        # absolute
        prefix = _random_abs_prefix(r)
        is_windows = ("\\" in prefix)
        parts.append(prefix.rstrip("/\\"))
    else:
        # relative
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(".")
        elif r.random() < 0.2:
            parts.append("..")
    depth = r.randint(1, 4)
    common_dirs = [
        "rime", "data", "shared", "user", "config", "schemas", "build", "staging",
    ]
    for i in range(depth):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_choice(r, common_dirs))
        else:
            parts.append(_random_name(r))
    return _join_path(parts, is_windows)

def _random_file_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = _random_dir_path(r)
    # Ensure separator at end
    is_windows = ("\\" in base and not base.startswith("/"))
    sep = "\\" if is_windows else "/"
    fname_core = _random_name(r)
    # Occasionally generate common config filenames Rime uses
    if r.random() < 0.35:
        fname_core = _weighted(r, [
            (3, "default"), (3, "user"), (2, "installation"), (2, "schema"),
            (1, "luna_pinyin"), (1, "terra_pinyin"), (1, "symbols"),
        ])
    ext = _random_ext(r)
    return base.rstrip("/\\") + sep + f"{fname_core}.{ext}"

def _interesting_fixed_paths(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Useful fixed paths to hit special cases
    win_base = "C:\\ProgramData\\Rime"
    user_base = os.path.expanduser("~") or "~/"
    posix_base = "/usr/share/rime"
    tmp = "/tmp" if os.name != "nt" else os.getenv("TMP", "C:\\Temp")
    return [
        posix_base,
        f"{posix_base}/build",
        f"{posix_base}/prebuilt",
        f"{user_base}/.config/rime",
        f"{user_base}/Library/Rime" if os.name == "darwin" else f"{user_base}/AppData/Roaming/Rime",
        win_base,
        os.path.join(tmp, "rime_test.yaml").replace("\\", "/"),
    ]

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    paths: List[str] = []

    # Mix of directory-like strings for traits and schema/config APIs
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        paths.append(_random_dir_path(r))

    # Mix of filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME usage (export/import)
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        paths.append(_random_file_path(r))

    # Add some fixed, well-known locations
    paths.extend(_interesting_fixed_paths(r))

    # Ensure uniqueness and keep size under limit
    dedup: List[str] = []
    seen = set()
    for p in paths:
        if p not in seen and p:
            seen.add(p)
            dedup.append(p)

    # Shuffle deterministically with the seed
    r.shuffle(dedup)

    # Join as newline-separated list; consumers can pick first or iterate
    out = "\n".join(dedup)

    # Trim to 4096 bytes if necessary by dropping tail entries
    encoded = out.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(encoded) > 4096:
        # Drop entries until it fits
        while dedup and len("\n".join(dedup).encode('utf-8')) > 4096:
            dedup.pop()
        encoded = "\n".join(dedup).encode('utf-8')

    return encoded

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for: filesystem path with arbitrary file data
# Target fuzzers use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() and FUZZ_PARAM_STR().
# The harness provides a temporary file populated with our returned bytes, and
# passes its path to the API. To exercise different code paths, we embed a tiny
# container format that can carry:
#  - A candidate dictionary name (ASCII/UTF-8) for import_user_dict
#  - A format/tag header to hint at expected import formats (plain, TSV, YAML-like)
#  - Multiple record lines with varied encodings, lengths, and edge characters
#  - Optional BOMs, comments, and metadata lines
# The same bytes are also suitable for restore_user_dict, which only needs a readable file.
#
# File layout (all text UTF-8 unless prefixed with BOM):
#  - Optional UTF-8 BOM
#  - Header line: "FMT:<fmt>;DICT:<name>;FLAGS:<flagstr>\n"
#  - Zero or more metadata/comment lines starting with '#'
#  - Payload section depending on <fmt>:
#     * plain: lines of words/phrases
#     * tsv:   tab-separated entries: key\tvalue\tweight\tcomment
#     * yaml:  minimal YAML-like document that some importers may parse as config
#  - Trailing newline and a possible NUL to test robust readers
# All bytes length kept <= 4096.

FMT_PLAIN = "plain"
FMT_TSV = "tsv"
FMT_YAML = "yaml"

MAX_SIZE = 4096

ASCII_WORDS = [
    "hello", "world", "test", "rime", "input", "method",
    "pinyin", "zhuyin", "schema", "custom", "user", "dict",
]

UNICODE_WORDS = [
    "你好", "世界", "输入法", "測試", "繁體", "简体", "拼音", "注音",
    "漢字", "词库", "😀", "éclair", "naïve", "русский",
]

# Hot characters often present in dictionaries
EDGE_CHARS = ["'", "-", "·", ".", ",", ";", ":", "/", "\\", "_", "~"]


def _rand(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(seq)


def _maybe(rng: random.Random, p: float) -> bool:
    return rng.random() < p


def _rand_word(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if _maybe(rng, 0.5):
        base = _rand(rng, ASCII_WORDS)
        # Maybe add edge chars
        if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
            base = base + _rand(rng, EDGE_CHARS)
        if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
            base = _rand(rng, EDGE_CHARS) + base
        return base
    else:
        w = _rand(rng, UNICODE_WORDS)
        if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
            w = w + _rand(rng, EDGE_CHARS)
        return w


def _rand_phrase(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(1, 5)
    return " ".join(_rand_word(rng) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_dict_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common dictionary names and variations
    bases = [
        "user", "custom", "symbols", "emoji", "pinyin", "zhuyin", "luna", "terra"
    ]
    suffix = _rand(rng, ["_dict", "_userdb", "_personal", "_addon", "_lex"])
    name = _rand(rng, bases) + suffix
    # Maybe include hyphen or dot
    if _maybe(rng, 0.3):
        name = name + _rand(rng, ["-ext", ".v1", ".backup", "-alt"])  
    return name


def _gen_header(rng: random.Random, fmt: str, dict_name: str, flags: List[str]) -> str:
    flagstr = ",".join(flags)
    return f"FMT:{fmt};DICT:{dict_name};FLAGS:{flagstr}\n"


def _gen_comments(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 5)):
        key = _rand(rng, ["generator", "encoding", "version", "author", "date"])  
        val = _rand_phrase(rng)
        lines.append(f"# {key}: {val}\n")
    return "".join(lines)


def _gen_plain_payload(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    lines = []
    count = rng.randint(5, 200)
    for _ in range(count):
        line = _rand_phrase(rng)
        if _maybe(rng, 0.1):
            # Add inline comment
            line += "  # " + _rand_word(rng)
        lines.append(line + "\n")
    return "".join(lines)


def _gen_tsv_payload(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common TSV format used by some Rime importers: word<TAB>code<TAB>weight<TAB>comment
    lines = []
    count = rng.randint(5, 200)
    for _ in range(count):
        word = _rand_word(rng)
        # Compose a plausible code (e.g., pinyin or letter code)
        code_len = rng.randint(1, 6)
        code = "".join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase) for _ in range(code_len))
        weight = str(rng.randint(1, 10000)) if _maybe(rng, 0.8) else ""
        comment = _rand_phrase(rng) if _maybe(rng, 0.2) else ""
        fields = [word, code, weight, comment]
        # Trim trailing empties to vary field counts
        while fields and fields[-1] == "":
            fields.pop()
        line = "\t".join(fields) + "\n"
        lines.append(line)
    return "".join(lines)


def _gen_yaml_payload(rng: random.Random, dict_name: str) -> str:
    # Minimal YAML-like dictionary export. Even if not parsed as YAML by importer,
    # it's still valid text content to read.
    entries = []
    n = rng.randint(3, 50)
    for _ in range(n):
        k = _rand_word(rng)
        v = _rand_phrase(rng)
        # Escape colon-heavy values minimally
        if ":" in v:
            v = f'"{v}"'
        entries.append(f"  - key: {k}\n    value: {v}\n")
    yaml_doc = [
        f"dict: {dict_name}\n",
        "format: rime-yaml\n",
        "entries:\n",
        "".join(entries),
    ]
    return "".join(yaml_doc)


def _apply_bom_and_terminators(rng: random.Random, data: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Optional BOM
    if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
        data = b"\xEF\xBB\xBF" + data
    # Optional trailing newline(s)
    if _maybe(rng, 0.7):
        data += b"\n"
        if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
            data += b"\n"
    # Optional final NUL
    if _maybe(rng, 0.1):
        data += b"\x00"
    return data


def _cap_size(buf: bytes) -> bytes:
    if len(buf) <= MAX_SIZE:
        return buf
    # Keep header and crop payload smartly: keep first 3KB and last 0.5KB
    head = buf[:3072]
    tail = buf[-512:]
    mid = b"\n# truncated\n"
    combined = head + mid + tail
    return combined[:MAX_SIZE]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a format and flags to guide the importer
    fmt = rng.choice([FMT_PLAIN, FMT_TSV, FMT_YAML])
    dict_name = _rand_dict_name(rng)
    flags = []
    if _maybe(rng, 0.4):
        flags.append("utf8")
    if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
        flags.append("with_weights")
    if _maybe(rng, 0.2):
        flags.append("comments")
    if _maybe(rng, 0.15):
        flags.append("sorted")

    parts: List[str] = []
    parts.append(_gen_header(rng, fmt, dict_name, flags))
    parts.append(_gen_comments(rng))

    if fmt == FMT_PLAIN:
        parts.append(_gen_plain_payload(rng))
    elif fmt == FMT_TSV:
        parts.append(_gen_tsv_payload(rng))
    else:  # yaml
        parts.append(_gen_yaml_payload(rng, dict_name))

    text = "".join(parts)
    data = text.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")
    data = _apply_bom_and_terminators(rng, data)
    data = _cap_size(data)
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: "application name" used in RimeTraits.app_name and logging setup.
# The fuzz stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times to populate fields like
# shared_data_dir, user_data_dir, distribution fields, and app_name.
# Our generator should return a single bytes buffer that the harness will split to
# satisfy multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls. We therefore pack a sequence of NUL-terminated
# strings in one buffer. Each call to FUZZ_PARAM_STR() will read the next string.
#
# Goals for valid/interesting values:
# - Provide plausible directory-like paths for shared/user data dirs.
# - Provide app names in both plain and legacy "rime.x" style to exercise different code paths.
# - Include distribution fields (name/code/version) with typical and edge-ish yet valid content.
# - Keep inputs ASCII/UTF-8 and null-terminated; avoid malformed data.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# The first fuzzer stub needs 6 strings (shared_dir, user_dir, dist_name, dist_code, dist_ver, app_name).
# The second and third stubs each re-run setup with 3 strings (shared_dir, user_dir, app_name).
# The harness may request more strings later (e.g., YAML for config_load_string). We thus include
# extra strings like a short YAML snippet and a few generic names so future FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls
# still receive valid content.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _rand_choice_weighted(r: random.Random, items: List[str], extra_gen=None, extra_weight: int = 0) -> str:
    # Choose among predefined items or generate using extra_gen with a given weight
    if extra_gen and extra_weight > 0:
        idx = r.randrange(len(items) + extra_weight)
        if idx >= len(items):
            return extra_gen()
        return items[idx]
    return r.choice(items)

def _rand_component(r: random.Random, min_len=3, max_len=10) -> str:
    letters = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_"
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(r.choice(letters) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_version(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Semantic-like versions with optional pre-release/build metadata
    major = r.randint(0, 10)
    minor = r.randint(0, 20)
    patch = r.randint(0, 50)
    ver = f"{major}.{minor}.{patch}"
    # Occasionally add suffix
    choices = ["", "-alpha", "-beta", "-rc1", "+build" + str(r.randint(1, 100))]
    ver += r.choice(choices)
    return ver

def _rand_dir(r: random.Random, root_opts: List[str]) -> str:
    # Build a plausible UNIX-like path; may also produce Windows-like drive paths sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        # Windows-like
        drive = r.choice(list(string.ascii_uppercase))
        parts = [_rand_component(r, 3, 8) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))]
        return drive + ":\\" + "\\".join(parts)
    # Unix-like
    base = r.choice(root_opts)
    parts = [_rand_component(r, 3, 10) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3))]
    return base + "/".join(parts)

def _rand_app_name(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix of plain names and legacy rime.x style
    plain_candidates = [
        "rime.app",
        "ime-demo",
        "pinyin-tool",
        "input-method",
        "editor-plugin",
        "myapp",
        "rime.test",
    ]
    def gen_plain():
        return _rand_component(r, 4, 12)
    name = _rand_choice_weighted(r, plain_candidates, gen_plain, extra_weight=3)
    if r.random() < 0.5:

def _rand_yaml(r: random.Random) -> str:

def _nul_join(strings: List[str]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for s in strings:

        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL:

    return bytes(out[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets YAML data consumed by api->config_load_string in the RimeConfig fuzzer stub.
# Goal: produce valid, interesting YAML documents exercising maps, sequences, scalars, anchors,
# aliases, multi-line scalars, numbers, booleans, nulls, nested structures, and varying sizes.
# Output must be <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_BYTES = 4096

SCHEMA_IDS = [
    "luna_pinyin", "luna_pinyin_simp", "terra_pinyin", "cangjie5",
    "bopomofo", "stroke", "wubi86", "double_pinyin", "ipa_xsampa",
]

BOOLS = ["true", "false", "True", "False", "yes", "no", "on", "off"]
NULLS = ["null", "~", "Null", "NULL", ""]

# Some keys common in Rime YAMLs to increase likelihood of valid paths
COMMON_KEYS = [
    "schema", "schema_id", "name", "version", "author", "description",
    "engine", "processors", "segmentors", "translators", "filters",
    "speller", "translator", "punctuator", "key_binder", "recognizer",
    "menu", "page_size", "switches", "style", "ascii_composer",
    "punctuation", "switcher", "hotkeys", "dependencies",
]

PROCESSORS = [
    "ascii_composer", "recognizer", "key_binder", "speller",
    "punctuator", "selector", "navigator", "express_editor",
]
SEGMENTORS = [
    "ascii_segmentor", "matcher", "abc_segmentor", "punct_segmentor",
    "fallback_segmentor"
]
TRANSLATORS = [
    "table_translator", "punct_translator", "reverse_lookup_translator",
    "history_translator", "script_translator"
]
FILTERS = [
    "simplifier", "uniquifier", "reverse_lookup_filter", "charset_filter",
    "cjk_minifier"
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "omega", "zhong", "guo",
    "input", "method", "rime", "schema", "custom", "user",
]


def rand_ident(rng: random.Random, base_keys: List[str]) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.6 and base_keys:
        return rng.choice(base_keys)
    s = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase)
    n = rng.randint(0, 10)
    for _ in range(n):
        s += rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "_-")
    return s


def yaml_scalar(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    t = rng.random()
    if t < 0.18:
        return str(rng.randint(-100000, 100000))
    if t < 0.36:
        return rng.choice(BOOLS)
    if t < 0.44:
        return rng.choice(NULLS)
    if t < 0.62:
        # quoted string with escapes
        s = ' '.join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)))
        s = s.replace('"', '\\"')
        return f'"{s}"'
    if t < 0.78:
        # single-quoted
        s = ' '.join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)))
        s = s.replace("'", "''")
        return f"'{s}'"
    if t < 0.9:
        # plain scalar
        return ' '.join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 5)))
    # multiline literal or folded
    style = '|' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '>'
    lines = []
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
        lines.append(' '.join(rng.choice(WORDS) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 6))))
    indented = '\n'.join('  ' + L for L in lines)
    return f"{style}\n{indented}"


def yaml_seq(rng: random.Random, depth: int, base_keys: List[str]) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(0, 6)
    items = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if depth > 0 and rng.random() < 0.35:
            items.append(indent_block(yaml_map(rng, depth - 1, base_keys), 2, dash=True))
        elif depth > 0 and rng.random() < 0.6:
            items.append(indent_block(yaml_seq(rng, depth - 1, base_keys), 2, dash=True))
        else:
            items.append(f"- {yaml_scalar(rng)}")
    return '\n'.join(items)


def indent_block(block: str, spaces: int, dash: bool = False) -> str:
    lines = block.split('\n')
    if not lines:
        return "-" if dash else ""
    if dash:
        # first line with dash, rest further indented
        out = ["- " + lines[0]]
        out.extend((' ' * (2)) + line for line in lines[1:])
        return '\n'.join(out)
    return '\n'.join((' ' * spaces) + line if line else line for line in lines)


def yaml_map(rng: random.Random, depth: int, base_keys: List[str]) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(3, 10)
    used = set()
    lines = []
    anchors = []
    # optionally define an anchor
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        akey = rand_ident(rng, base_keys)
        aval = yaml_scalar(rng)
        lines.append(f"{akey}: &{akey}_a {aval}")
        anchors.append(akey)
        used.add(akey)
    for _ in range(n):
        key = rand_ident(rng, base_keys)
        if key in used:
            key += '_' + str(rng.randint(1, 999))
        used.add(key)
        choice = rng.random()
        if depth > 0 and choice < 0.25:
            # nested map
            lines.append(f"{key}:")
            nested = yaml_map(rng, depth - 1, base_keys)
            lines.append(indent_block(nested, 2))
        elif depth > 0 and choice < 0.45:
            # nested sequence
            lines.append(f"{key}:")
            seq = yaml_seq(rng, depth - 1, base_keys)
            lines.append(indent_block(seq, 2))
        elif anchors and choice < 0.55:
            # alias
            a = rng.choice(anchors)
            lines.append(f"{key}: *{a}_a")
        else:
            lines.append(f"{key}: {yaml_scalar(rng)}")
    return '\n'.join(lines)


def rime_like_document(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Construct a document resembling a Rime schema/config
    schema_id = rng.choice(SCHEMA_IDS)
    name = schema_id.replace('_', ' ').title()
    doc_parts = []

    header = [
        "schema:",
        f"  schema_id: {schema_id}",
        f"  name: '{name}'",
        f"  version: '{rng.randint(1, 3)}.{rng.randint(0, 9)}.{rng.randint(0, 9)}'",
        f"  author: '{rng.choice(['lotem','user','tester'])}'",
        "  description: >",
        "    A generated schema for exercising librime config loader.",
    ]
    doc_parts.extend(header)

    # engine section
    procs = rng.sample(PROCESSORS, k=rng.randint(2, min(5, len(PROCESSORS))))
    segs = rng.sample(SEGMENTORS, k=rng.randint(2, min(4, len(SEGMENTORS))))
    trans = rng.sample(TRANSLATORS, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(TRANSLATORS))))
    filts = rng.sample(FILTERS, k=rng.randint(1, min(3, len(FILTERS))))

    def yaml_array(name: str, items: List[str]) -> List[str]:
        lines = [f"  {name}:"]
        for x in items:
            lines.append(f"    - {x}")
        return lines

    doc_parts.append("engine:")
    doc_parts += yaml_array("processors", procs)
    doc_parts += yaml_array("segmentors", segs)
    doc_parts += yaml_array("translators", trans)
    doc_parts += yaml_array("filters", filts)

    # menu and style
    doc_parts.append("menu:")
    doc_parts.append(f"  page_size: {rng.randint(3, 9)}")
    doc_parts.append("style:")
    doc_parts.append(f"  horizontal: {rng.choice(BOOLS)}")
    doc_parts.append(f"  inline_preedit: {rng.choice(BOOLS)}")

    # switches
    doc_parts.append("switches:")
    for key in [
        ("ascii_mode", "ASCII mode"),
        ("full_shape", "Full width"),
        ("simplification", "Simplify"),
    ]:
        k, n = key
        doc_parts.append("  - name: " + k)
        doc_parts.append("    reset: 0")
        doc_parts.append("    states:")
        doc_parts.append("      - off")
        doc_parts.append("      - on")
        doc_parts.append("    reset_on_commit: " + rng.choice(BOOLS))

    # recognizer and key_binder with hotkeys
    doc_parts.append("recognizer:")
    doc_parts.append("  patterns:")
    doc_parts.append("    email: '[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\\\.[A-Za-z]{2,}'")
    doc_parts.append("key_binder:")
    doc_parts.append("  import_preset: default")
    doc_parts.append("  bindings:")
    for k in ["Control+Shift+1", "Control+grave", "Shift+space"]:
        doc_parts.append("    - when: composing")
        doc_parts.append(f"      accept: '{k}'")
        doc_parts.append("      toggle: ascii_mode")

    # user overrides map with nested structures and anchors
    doc_parts.append("customization:")
    nested = yaml_map(rng, depth=2, base_keys=COMMON_KEYS)
    doc_parts.append(indent_block(nested, 2))

    # An optional document trailer with random content
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        doc_parts.append("# extra:")
        doc_parts.append(yaml_seq(rng, depth=2, base_keys=COMMON_KEYS) or "-")

    return '\n'.join(doc_parts) + '\n'


def assemble_documents(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    docs = []
    # 1..3 documents separated by --- to exercise multi-doc parsing
    for i in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            docs.append("---\n" + rime_like_document(rng))
        else:
            # generic map-heavy document
            docs.append("---\n" + yaml_map(rng, depth=3, base_keys=COMMON_KEYS) + "\n")
    # sometimes add explicit end marker
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        docs.append("...\n")
    text = ''.join(docs)
    if len(text.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_BYTES:
        # trim safely on byte length boundary
        b = text.encode('utf-8')[:MAX_BYTES]
        # ensure we end with newline for YAML doc completeness
        if not b.endswith(b"\n"):
            b = b.rstrip(b"\r\n") + b"\n"
        return b.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
    return text


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    yaml_text = assemble_documents(rng)
    # Ensure non-empty and valid UTF-8 bytes
    data = yaml_text.encode('utf-8')
    if not data:
        data = b"schema:\n  schema_id: test\n"
    # Final cap
    if len(data) > MAX_BYTES:
        data = data[:MAX_BYTES]
        if not data.endswith(b"\n"):
            data += b"\n"
    return data
